subject: biology
source_note: Topic structure follows the National Curriculum KS3 programme of study for Biology. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Structure & Function of Living Organisms
units.blurb: Cells, organ systems, reproduction and health in humans and plants

units.name: Material Cycles & Energy
units.blurb: How organisms capture, store and release energy

units.name: Interactions & Interdependencies
units.blurb: How organisms depend on one another in ecosystems

units.name: Genetics & Evolution
units.blurb: Inheritance, variation, natural selection and biodiversity

topics.name: Cells & Organisation
topics.blurb: Cell structure, organelles, diffusion and the cells-to-organisms hierarchy

topics.name: Skeletal & Muscular Systems
topics.blurb: The human skeleton, biomechanics and antagonistic muscles

topics.name: Nutrition & Digestion
topics.blurb: A balanced diet, the digestive system, enzymes and gut bacteria

topics.name: Gas Exchange Systems
topics.blurb: Breathing, the lungs, the effect of exercise and smoking, leaf stomata

topics.name: Reproduction
topics.blurb: Human and plant reproduction, fertilisation, gestation and dispersal

topics.name: Health
topics.blurb: Effects of recreational drugs on behaviour and life processes

topics.name: Photosynthesis
topics.blurb: Reactants, products and the dependence of life on photosynthesis

topics.name: Cellular Respiration
topics.blurb: Aerobic and anaerobic respiration and fermentation

topics.name: Relationships in an Ecosystem
topics.blurb: Food webs, pollination, food security and toxic accumulation

topics.name: Inheritance, Chromosomes, DNA & Genes
topics.blurb: Heredity, the DNA model, variation, natural selection and biodiversity

connections.why: Specialised cells build the tissues and organs of the skeleton and muscles
The digestive system is an organ system built from specialised tissues
Diffusion across cell membranes underlies gas exchange in the lungs and leaves
Digestion supplies the glucose that respiration breaks down for energy
Breathing delivers the oxygen aerobic respiration needs and removes carbon dioxide
Glucose made in photosynthesis is the fuel respiration releases
Leaf stomata exchange the carbon dioxide and oxygen photosynthesis uses and makes
Chloroplasts are the organelles where photosynthesis happens
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through every food web
Insect pollination links plant reproduction to ecosystems and food security
Gametes pass genetic information from one generation to the next
Chromosomes carrying DNA are stored in the cell nucleus
Variation drives competition and natural selection within ecosystems
Diet and substances taken in affect health and life processes
Muscles need energy from respiration to contract and move the skeleton
